classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish total alloy mass from iron mass, express percentage contributions in a second equation and solve the routine simultaneous system.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by introducing two pronumerals and forming a pair of simultaneous equations.

One alloy of iron contains 52% iron and another contains 36% iron. How many tonnes of each alloy should be used to make 200 tonnes of 40% iron alloy?

answer.short:
50 tonnes of the 52% iron alloy and 150 tonnes of the 36% iron alloy.

Form equations for the total mass and the mass of iron, then use elimination.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the mass in tonnes of the 52% iron alloy and $y$ the mass in tonnes of the 36% iron alloy.
$$\begin{align*}x+y&=200 &&\text{(1)}\\0.52x+0.36y&=0.40\times200\\52x+36y&=8000 &&\text{(2)}\end{align*}$$
Multiply equation (1) by 36, then subtract it from equation (2):
$$\begin{align*}36x+36y&=7200\\(52x+36y)-(36x+36y)&=8000-7200\\16x&=800\\x&=50\end{align*}$$
Substitute into equation (1):
$$\begin{align*}50+y&=200\\y&=150\end{align*}$$
Check: $50+150=200$ tonnes and $0.52\times50+0.36\times150=26+54=80$ tonnes of iron, which is $40\%$ of $200$ tonnes.

Use 50 tonnes of the 52% iron alloy and 150 tonnes of the 36% iron alloy.
